rationale: While early and several subsequent cohorts report near-complete penetrance of speech delay and language impairment in FBXO11-related neurodevelopmental disorder (e.g., 23/23 in PanelApp curation data and 20/21 [95%] in preprint cohorts, clearly outperforming facial dysmorphism and behavioral issues in sensitivity), replication in expanded independent cohorts demonstrates incomplete penetrance. Specifically, Pan et al. (2024) identified speech and language development delay in only 8 of 12 affected individuals (66.7%) from 5 Chinese families harboring pathogenic FBXO11 variants, while intellectual disability was present in 12/12 (100%) and global developmental delay in 10/12 (83.3%). Consequently, the hypothesis that speech delay consistently exhibits >=95% penetrance across all independent cohorts is directly contradicted.

evidence.text: In a study of 12 affected individuals from 5 Chinese families with FBXO11-associated neurodevelopmental disorder, speech and language development delay was documented in only 8 of 12 individuals (66.7%), whereas intellectual disability was universal (12/12, 100%) and global developmental delay was observed in 10/12 (83.3%).

In Pan et al. (2024), intellectual disability was present in 100% (12/12) and global developmental delay in 83.3% (10/12), demonstrating that general cognitive delay/ID can have higher clinical sensitivity than speech impairment in certain familial cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Does speech impairment penetrance in FBXO11 disorder differ between familial/inherited hypomorphic variants versus de novo loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Familial cases like those in Pan et al. (2024) showed reduced penetrance of speech delay (66.7%), whereas de novo truncating and severe missense cohorts showed 95-100% speech delay. Stratifying penetrance by inheritance and variant class will clarify diagnostic utility.

new_directions.question_text: What is the discriminant diagnostic performance of speech impairment compared to comorbid features (autism, hypotonia, facial dysmorphism) when distinguishing FBXO11 from other F-box neurodevelopmental disorders such as FBXW7?
new_directions.rationale: FBXW7 and other related ubiquitination pathway disorders present with overlapping global delay and hypotonia; evaluating whether speech delay has specificity or just high sensitivity is crucial for differential diagnosis.
